question: The energy currency of the cell is called as:
solution:
Correct answer is __**ATP.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adenosine triphosphate, or ATP**, is the chief molecule for storing and transferring energy in cells.
 
• The structure of ATP is a **nucleoside triphosphate, **made up of a nitrogenous base (adenine), a ribose sugar, and three serially bonded phosphate groups.
 
• ATP is generally mentioned as the** "energy currency" **of the cell, as **it provides readily releasable energy in the bond between the second and third phosphate groups**.
 
• ATP plays an important role in the **transport of macromolecules such as proteins and lipids into and out of the cell**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adenosine monophosphate** (AMP) is one of the components of RNA and also the organic component of the energy-carrying molecule ATP.​
 
• Ribonucleic acid (RNA) is **a nucleic acid present in all living cells that has structural similarities to DNA**. 
 
• DNA, or **deoxyribonucleic acid**, is the hereditary material in humans and nearly all other organisms.
